\subsection{Simulation on Replayed Production Sessions}\label{sec:sim}

The simulator replays the production sessions of \S\ref{sec:exp-traces}
against a simulated replica: decode is a bandwidth PS with the
demand~\eqref{eq:decode}, prefill a FIFO server on the compute the
batch leaves, resident KV a prefix that a turn re-prefills with the
work~\eqref{eq:prefill} once evicted. The workload side is measured, and the cost model is the one fitted on
the NPU testbed in \S\ref{sec:exp-testbed}: the prefill terms of E1
and a decode iteration of $\omega=\simCalOmega$\,s, the mean
inter-token latency of the E2 replays, which did not vary with the
context ($\beta=0$); so the replica is simulated at the measured
costs, but no number here is a measurement of a serving system.
Before the replay, every proposition is checked as a seeded test under
its own assumptions and with one assumption dropped
(Appendix~\ref{app:sim}; \simChecksPassed{} of \simChecks{} checks
pass): the closed forms are reproduced within 2\,\% or their
confidence intervals; forced misses land at the upper end of the
bracket of Proposition~\ref{prop:price} and raise the prefill queue
while leaving the decode batch unchanged; the priced eviction orders
beat shortest-first only within seed noise while the admission cap
decides whether the replica thrashes; and over four replicas the load
at which moving beats affinity follows $\rho^*$ of~\eqref{eq:rhostar}
for a fast link.

\paragraph{Replayed production sessions.} Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace}
(Appendix~\ref{app:sim}) plays each real session's appends, outputs, think times and length on
the replica; a gap above ten minutes starts a new session whose first
prompt is the accumulated context (splitting at thirty minutes changes
$W_q$, the PK wait and TTFT within seed noise,
Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace-split}). With no eviction every follow-up turn
hits and its prefill work still has
$\mathrm{CV}^2=\simTraceOpenCvMin$--$\simTraceOpenCvMax$ from the
appends alone, while the mean TTFT of
\simTraceOpenTtftMin--\simTraceOpenTtftMax\,s is set by the cold first
prompts. Once the pool is finite the cap on live sessions binds, the
replica is a closed system of $N$ sessions and the entry queue grows
for the whole horizon; at the tight cap the hit rate stays at or above
\simTraceTightHitMin{} and the hit/miss mixture supplies
\simTraceTightMixMin--\simTraceTightMixMax\,\% of the variance of
follow-up prefill work, at the loose cap the replica thrashes (hit rate
at most \simTraceLooseHitMax, mean TTFT above
\simTraceLooseTtftMin\,s). The PK wait from the measured $\lambda$,
$\E[S]$ and $\E[S^2]$ is above the observed wait in every cell, by
\simTracePkRatioMin{} to \simTracePkRatioMax{} times, as
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite} says it must for exponential work. For
the price itself, Table~\ref{tab:sim-trace-price} forces a share
$\delta$ of resident follow-up turns to miss and compares the rise of
the number in the prefill stage with the bracket of
Proposition~\ref{prop:price} and with the finite-source price of
Proposition~\ref{prop:finite}: with \simPriceLiveMin{} to
\simPriceLiveMax{} sessions live, the open bracket's lower end
overstates the rise by \simPriceOverMin{} to \simPriceOverMax{} times,
at the higher rate and $\delta\ge3\,\%$ the added work puts the open
queue past its pole while the capped replica stays finite, the Markovian finite-source price, which
ignores the second moment of the work, understates the rise by
\simPriceFiniteRatioMin{} to \simPriceFiniteRatioMax{} times, and the
cap $N-L_P$ holds in \simPriceCapHolds{} cell. The real rise lies between the two prices.
